By Ian Putzger Americas correspondent
4 November 2026
Airport cargo infrastructure, as well as established ways of handling logistics, are being challenged by growing traffic.
Airfreight capacity between Latin America and Canada is on the rise, courtesy of Air Canada (AC).
Last month, the airline resumed service to Santiago and Lima, serving the Chilean capital with four weekly nonstop flights each from Montreal and Toronto with B787-9 aircraft – the only carrier with direct flights on these routes.
AC’s return to the Peruvian market, twice weekly out of Toronto and Montreal with B787-9s, ended a three-year hiatus. The airline also deployed the aircraft type on its route to Bogota, marking an increase in capacity from the A330 previously used.
Elsewhere in the region, AC firmed up its presence in Guatemala. Nonstop flights with A330s between Montreal and Guatemala City, launched in October 2025 on a seasonal basis, have been extended to year-round operation.
Indeed, Latin America is seeing a steady influx of international carriers, partly drawn by open skies policies in Argentina and Ecuador.
According to one report, Ethiopian Airlines is considering cargo flights to Buenos Aires, utilising traffic rights that include cabotage. Emirates, which has established itself as a major presence in the region, stepped up its Buenos Aires freighter operation to seven a week this year. It registered 18% growth in exports from the region for the January-September period.
In the first half of this year, cargo volumes out of Latin America grew 3.6%, according to IATA. And statistics from the Latin American and Caribbean Air Transport Association (ALTA) show the momentum continued through July, led by Brazil and Colombia with annual growth of 9.8% and 8.4% respectively.
The pace increased in August, with tonnages up 11.8% out of Brazil and Colombia. In percentage terms, Argentina was the leader in August, showing 17% growth in volume.
While cause for celebration, these numbers are also producing some headaches. ALTA CEO Peter Cerda, warned that this growth was on a collision course with capacity constraints. He stated that 54% of the airports in the region were already showing signs of saturation.
Future growth will depend to a large extent on the ability of governments and airport authorities to accelerate infrastructure investment, he stressed. Among the airports that need expansion and modernisation to be able to absorb growth, he highlighted Sao Paulo’s Guarulhos, alongside Bogota, Lima, and Santiago.
On a positive note, airport operator Servicios Aeroportuarios Andinos (SAASA), which recently started constructing its second cargo terminal at Madrid’s Adolfo Suarez Airport, has signalled plans to expand further in Latin America, looking at Argentina, Chile, and Colombia for ramp and cargo services.
At Lima’s Jorge Chavez Airport, SAASA has spent more than $1m to ramp up import and export capabilities, and management is looking at doubling its capacity by 2030.
Currently, operations at Buenos Aires Ezeiza Airport are hampered by infrastructure improvement work. The rehabilitation of its second runway involves work on the intersection with the main runwayuntil 11 November, which reduces its length from 3,300 metres to 1,850. This restricts operations of widebodies, a predicament that has prompted a number of carriers, including Atlas Air, American, and Lufthansa, to suspend Buenos Aires flights for the duration of the work. According to Rotate, capacity at Ezeiza has been cut by some 80%.
Port updates from Hillebrand-Gori show an indefinite trucker strike at Chile’s San Antonio port over rising fuel costs and toll expansions since 29 October. Of greater concern is the road connecting Mendoza in Argentina to Chilean ports, which has seen repeated and lengthy closures this season, resulting in severe delays.
Otherwise, port operations in Latin America have been stable, according to Maersk. However, in the carrier’s market update for October Alicia De La Guardia, head of digital marketing and digital sales, warned that landside operations were at a crossroads, with traffic growth stretching capacity and the established way of doing business.
Mordor Intelligence projects South America’s freight and logistics market to expand, from $270.18bn this year to $348.78bn by 2031. And Ms De La Guardia pointed to a study by McKinsey, which concluded that growth would depend on stronger infrastructure, additional trade corridors, and more integrated supply chains.
This required investment in road infrastructure as well as a change in business practices, she argued. The prevalent way of solving problems on the back of relationships – knowing somebody who can fix a problem – will no longer be adequate.
“Relationship-driven exception management can work well when volumes ae low, routes are familiar, and only a few scenarios need attention,” she said.
“But relying on this way of supply chain management breaks down under pressure – when market conditions change.”

Fiat Pandina and 500 Production Hindered by N3 GSE ECU Chip Shortage
12 photos
Photo: Fiat
Stellantis Europe has a problem on its hands. An electronic component destined for the N3 GSE engine's control unit has already disrupted October production of the Pandina and 500, and the consequences of this constraint may also extend to the facility where said powertrain is produced.
First and foremost, N3 GSE is part of the FireFly engine family. Displacing just under 1 liter, the three-pot mill is a naturally aspirated lump that started production back in 2016. The BSG version of the N3 GSE adds 12-volt assistance in the form of a small battery and a belt-driven starter generator. The BSG provides additional torque in certain scenarios, lowering the load on the engine.
As implied, the BSG serves as a generator when coasting or stepping on the brakes, harvesting kinetic energy that is directly fed into the lithium-ion battery. A coasting mode also needs to be highlighted, along with an ultra-quiet restart procedure when the driver presses the clutch pedal to select first gear. To further maximize efficiency, the BSG version runs on the Miller cycle.
Having cleared that up, this chip shortage could not have arrived at a worse time for Stellantis Europe. The Pandina , which is what Fiat calls the old-school Panda nowadays, moved plenty of units in October. Even though Fiat could not make as many as it wanted, the Pandina remained the best-selling car in the Italian automaker's home market, posting 7,198 sales last month.
The chip shortage puts Fiat in a very frustrating position because demand for the Pandina certainly is there. Stellantis Europe, however, cannot supply as freely as it would like. Also used by the hybridized 500, the engine control unit of the 1.0-liter mill does a lot of things. From core engine management to advanced energy orchestration, diagnostics, and self-preservation when a critical fault is detected, that control unit is one of the most important in a modern vehicle.
Photo: Fiat No fewer than three Italian manufacturing locations could feel the consequences of this particular shortage. Mirafiori is the plant where Fiat makes the 500 Hybrid, whereas Pomigliano d'Arco builds the Pandina. Both models come as mild hybrids by default nowadays, and the 500 can also be had with full-electric propulsion.
Beyond said factories, Termoli is where the N3 GSE inline-three is assembled. Stellantis Europe has yet to announce downtime for Termoli, and the company hasn't quantified the expected production losses either. As of this writing, Fiat and Stellantis are working hard with suppliers to identify alternatives in order to progressively restore normal production outputs.
Speaking of disruptions, the Mirafiori plant had already entered a separate three-week stoppage in October due to an unrelated shortage. Weak demand for the 500 line also contributed to said interruption, and the latest shortage introduces yet another constraint at a plant that was already struggling to maintain its designated production schedule.
Looking at the bigger picture, Stellantis and Fiat should have known better. The industry already went through a far more painful version of this problem in 2021 and 2022, with US light vehicle production recovering to pre-crisis levels in early 2023. Back then, automakers responded by prioritizing higher-margin vehicles, deleting semiconductor-dependent features that were not absolutely essential.
On a related note, Stellantis has recently said that its 2026 financial guidance remains unchanged following its third-quarter results. Stellantis also maintained expectations for positive industrial free cash flow in 2027, meaning that Stellantis isn't forecasting any significant revisions linked to this chip shortage.

Cadillac F1 Team Reportedly Up for Sale and the Asking Price Is $3 Billion
8 photos
Photo: Cadillac F1 Team
Well, that was fast. You know that old saying about where there's smoke, there's fire? Let's just say that things aren't looking particularly rosy for Mark Walter and his TWG Global group, with federal investigators scrutinizing billions of dollars in transactions involving his insurance businesses. We're talking potentially $20 billion here, which explains why Walter has been busy unloading high-profile sports assets since August.
From the outside, it looks like a deliberate effort to generate liquidity. First, Walter unloaded his controlling stake in the Los Angeles Lakers at a $12.5 billion valuation for the NBA franchise. That happened back in August. Then, in September, he sold his 12.8% stake in Chelsea Football Club. There's word on the street that the LA Sparks are up for grabs too, for around $700 million.
On top of that, Walter is reportedly looking to unload his controlling interest in Cadillac F1 Team, seeking around $3 billion for the American outfit. It seems as though the only asset he has no interest in unloading is the Los Angeles Dodgers MLB franchise. I don't blame him. They won back-to-back World Series titles in 2024 and 2025, and they're arguably the best-run franchise in American sports.
Is there a world where the Dodgers also end up on the auction block? Conceivably, yes. But we'll have to wait and see how things develop.
Back to Cadillac, the asking price is $3 billion according to three people familiar with the process, and there are at least seven parties interested in purchasing the team, as reported by Sportico . Walter's racing assets also include IndyCar and NASCAR teams.
What's interesting is that while TWG is the controlling owner in Cadillac F1 Team , the overall ownership breakdown remains unknown with General Motors and its Cadillac subsidiary in the mix as well. TWG and GM paid a $450 million fee and invested an additional $1 billion in a team that's on track to lose roughly $400 million this year - according to multiple sources.
Photo: Cadillac F1 Team Cadillac has been struggling a great deal in F1 in this maiden season of theirs, which was to be expected. They've yet to score a single point. On the plus side, Sergio Perez recently extended his contract with the team through 2029 (at the very least).
Is Cadillac F1 Team worth $3 billion? Seeing how the grid average for the 10 teams was $3.42 billion as recently as a year ago, I'd say that yes, that's a fair valuation for late 2026 or 2027 - whenever the reported sale might go through. It would also make the U.S. outfit more valuable, on paper, than Williams, Alpine, Racing Bulls, Kick Sauber and Haas. Nearly twice as valuable as Haas, that is... and about as valuable as Aston Martin.
Meanwhile, Ferrari tops the charts with a valuation north of $6 billion, which sounds about right.

US Auto Sales: Asian Automakers Like Honda, Hyundai, Kia, Subaru, or Mazda Support the Subtle Growth
7 photos
Photo: Honda
US automotive sales are subtly rebounding from the shocks of all the geopolitical unrest, but it's mainly because folks are now flocking to hybrids at an unprecedented rate due to high inflation and rising gasoline prices.
According to Automotive News, the US automotive market for new vehicles is reportedly expected to grow between four and seven percentage points as brands like Toyota, Honda, Hyundai, and Kia racked up solid gains in October thanks to continued strong retail demand for hybrids and crossover SUVs.
Out of the carmakers that have already reported their official numbers for October, American Honda achieved its best October month over the past six years thanks to record sales of light trucks and hybrid models. AHM grew sales by eight percent in October to 119,952 units for the best result since 2020. Honda totaled 109,162 units in October, up 9.1%, and even Acura posted solid October sales of 10,790 vehicles for a year-to-date total growth of almost 4%.
Year-to-date sales for American Honda stand at 1,269,213, up 5%, with Honda at 1,154,755 units. The brand sees the CR-V continue its fresh reign as the top-selling SUV in America while the Passport is on pace for a second consecutive record year. Now it’s time to switch to South Korea, as Hyundai had an excellent October and YTD result, too.
The company announced its best-ever October with 73,452 units and a 5% increase compared to last year. Overall, the ten-month performance is up by three percent to 770,916 units thanks to the massive push of the Santa Fe, Kona, Ioniq 5, Elantra, and Palisade. The Tucson remained on top with almost 200k units and a 6% increase. That’s great, since the siblings from Kia are breathing down their necks.
The cousin brand sold even more in October - 80,008 units- achieving a new record for the month after a massive 16% jump from last year. Electrified and hybrid vehicle sales increased 112 and 114 percent, respectively, and five models Telluride, Seltos, Carnival, K4, and Sportage each achieved best-ever October sales. The total for ten months is now at 747,394 units, up from 705,150 last year.
Back to Japanese brands, the folks over from Subaru are recovering from the slump earlier this year, posting a 6% increase in October to 54,090 vehicle sales led by Crosstrek and Forester going up both 26 percent in October. Even the WRX is up 55% year-to-date, but Subaru of America needs a continued punch to come out of the woods: year-to-date total sales are at 529,968, which is down almost one percent from last year.
Last but not least comes Mazda , with MNAO - Mazda North American Operations – reporting total October sales of 31,446 vehicles, an increase of 25 percent compared to last year and its second-best October deliveries. Year-to-date sales totaled 341,714 vehicles, which is also almost one percent down from last year after weak initial sales during the first part of the year.

source_document.body:
CHICAGO — Parcel shippers spent years handing one national carrier all their volume and negotiating once. At FarEye’s Last Mile Leaders America 2026 conference in August, panelists described why shippers are moving away from single-carrier agreements. Rising surcharges are part of the reason. Software that lets shippers manage multiple carriers has also made the shift easier.
Kyle Langley, Vice President of Final Mile at Tractor Supply Co., has watched that shift from the shipper side over about 15 years at the company. The rural lifestyle retailer has almost 2,500 stores in 49 states, and many of its delivery customers live on 5- to 15-acre properties. Tractor Supply now ships through parcel carriers, gig delivery networks and its own private fleet.
Langley shared the stage with Nick Costides, founder of C-Level Advisory and retired global president of information technology at UPS, and Brock Johns, Director Analyst at Gartner.
The panel moderator cited FarEye’s Eye on the Last Mile America 2026 report, released at the event, which found that 45.8% of U.S. delivery operators said delivery costs are rising faster than revenue . Including operators whose costs are keeping pace, 88% said delivery costs are growing as fast as revenue or faster . The same survey found that median last-mile costs rose 12% for a second year.
Carrier pricing now changes through surcharges as well as the annual general rate increase (GRI).
“Over the last couple of years, what we’ve seen coming out of small package is these variable charges that get applied in surcharges—not just surcharges, but how they define certain package types, big and bulky, and additional handling,” Langley said. “All those are somewhat unpredictable. GRI is not the only thing we have to worry about every year now.”
“Gone are the days when, as a retailer, we can kind of change our shipping and handling rates as changes come upstream from carriers,” he said. “We can’t do that. Customers want and expect reliable, standard shipping, and in a lot of cases, free.”
When one carrier applies surcharges to push bigger packages out of its network, Tractor Supply can redirect those packages to another carrier, he said, and limit the cost increase early in the year.
Splitting parcel volume by package type
The retailer moved to multiple parcel carriers about seven or eight years ago.
“We had a belief that if we give all of our volume to a single carrier, naturally that’s going to allow us more leverage to negotiate, and that’s not necessarily the case,” Langley said.
A single carrier blends a shipper’s whole package mix into one cost, he said, which can leave the biggest and smallest packages at unfavorable rates. Splitting the volume lets Tractor Supply decide which package types and regions go to which carrier.
Johns said using one carrier still works for some companies because it keeps pickups and procurement simple. Spreading volume costs a shipper some negotiating leverage overall, he said, and adds leverage in specific areas, along with flexibility.
How carriers tried to keep shippers
Costides traced the shift to the 1990s, when the first multi-carrier shipping software reached shipping desks and let administrators compare rates and transit times. Carriers noticed, he said.
“We tried to get our technology as far into companies’ supply chains as possible. That’s what happened,” Costides said. “You couldn’t switch because we were in too deep, and it was too expensive to leave.”
Two demand shocks loosened that grip, he said: the 2013 e-commerce surge that outran carrier forecasts before Christmas, and the supply chain crisis of the COVID-19 pandemic.
“So technology was the great equalizer, and it took an e-commerce hockey stick and a geopolitical crisis to actually accelerate this move and take the power out of carriers’ hands,” he said.
A carrier cannot successfully sell carrier-neutral technology itself, Costides said.
“We couldn’t bring a product to market like FarEye and say, look, it’s better when it’s UPS, but we’re also enabling other carriers,” he said. “Nobody was going to give us competitor data”.
Costides noted that the Teamsters have already started campaigning for the 2028 contract and that UPS is shifting toward higher-margin healthcare business .
“I got a screw the other day. It was 99 cents,” Costides said. “There’s no way with a unionized workforce I could deliver a 99-cent screw in one day.”
Rate shopping and discount tiers
Parcel agreements often tie discounts to volume thresholds, Langley said, so someone has to watch each carrier’s volume to keep the account inside its tier.
Tractor Supply tried real-time rate shopping when orders entered its warehouse management system, setting its carrier agreements against each other for the lowest cost on each package.
But that created a volume-balancing problem, Langley said.
“Because if all of a sudden too much volume shifts into one, well then you’re going down a discount tier with another carrier, and then it’s a self-fulfilling prophecy,” he said. “Then all the volume before you know it is just going to get eaten by that carrier that won originally.”
Choosing the cheapest carrier for each package does not always reduce overall shipping costs. Shifting too much volume away from another carrier can cost a shipper its negotiated discounts.
Managing those carrier agreements is work companies often overlook, Johns said.
“It’s a big step from just managing that one carrier to five, six, maybe ten, depending on where your strategy takes you,” he said. “We know it’s going to happen, but the amount of work and the time that goes into that is a different thing.”
A private fleet for rural delivery
Tractor Supply started its private fleet about two years ago, after adding gig networks for same-day and next-day service outside its parcel agreements. Langley said the fleet was meant to add a big-and-bulky service its customers did not have, with cost savings to follow.
“Our fleet is built to be able to take three or four pallets of horse feed to a 10-acre property and go into the stall, and our drivers know to go place it where the customer needs and what stall they need,” he said.
The retailer now handles deliveries from small packages to 10,000-pound loads. Third-party carriers still handle the smallest packages and the overflow, and Tractor Supply is adding more carriers for complex white-glove deliveries.
Putting service first is the one part of the launch Langley said he would not change.
“If you go the other way and you start low cost, low service, it’s very hard for an organization to have an appetite to increase costs over time to improve service,” he said. “So I would do it the same way ten out of ten times: start with service, and then have a three-year roadmap of how we’re going to claw back all that cost while not sacrificing your customer experience.”

A soldier holds a gun fitted with the ARBEL Anti-Drone System. (Photo Courtesy of IWI)
JERUSALEM — Small arms manufacturer Israel Weapons Industry is expanding its reach into Southeast Asia with four nations “currently at different stages of the procurement process” for its ARBEL Anti-Drone System, the company recently told Breaking Defense.
“We are seeing strong demand for our platforms and systems across the region,” the company said in response to questions about its growth strategy for southern Asia, where “countering the growing drone threat is one of the most pressing concerns our customers are raising.”
ARBEL is currently available for AR-15-type platforms, light machine guns and as an anti-drone system. This means soldiers can use it on existing rifle platforms they are already familiar with. It is also “optics-agnostic,” the company noted in an October statement.
Most recently, IWI, which is part of Israel’s SK Group, delivered the ARBEL ADS to Thailand’s Ministry of Defense, the company shared in an Oct. 22 statement.
“Following integration into its existing rifles and on-site training by IWI, the ARBEL ADS has been deployed and is now operational for day and night use,” the company said at the time.
As seen in the Ukraine-Russia war and the conflict between the US and Israel and Iran, small drone threats have been increasing, leading countries to seek out their own drone and counter-drone systems.
In the October statement, SK Group Vice President Doron Korol noted: “As Southeast Asian militaries place greater emphasis on counter-drone capabilities, Thailand’s adoption of ARBEL ADS reflects this growing operational priority. We see rising demand across the region for solutions that can help soldiers meet this challenge.”
SK Group’s Vice Chairman Ronen Hamudot added that “small tactical drones have become a direct and growing threat to soldiers on the battlefield.”
“While each country is moving at its own pace, the level of engagement reflects a broader shift in defense priorities across the region and the growing recognition that counter-drone capabilities are essential to modern military operations,” IWI said in last month’s statement.
Thailand integrated the system by replacing the lower receiver of existing rifles with the Arbel ADS system. “This approach enables militaries to upgrade their existing platforms locally without replacing their rifle inventories or procuring entirely new weapons,” IWI noted in its October statement.
IWI also said there are discussions with Thailand about additional orders.
In response to questions from Breaking Defense, the company said “This year alone, we conducted several ARBEL ADS demonstrations in Southeast Asian countries, reflecting growing interest in effective counter-drone solutions. Thailand’s deployment represents an important milestone, and we see significant potential to build on this momentum across the region.”
The company declined to disclose which other three Asian nations are in the process of procuring ARBEL systems. However, IWI told Breaking Defense that “the threat posed by small tactical drones is not confined to any one region, and Asian militaries face an increasingly complex security environment that includes terrorism, cross-border smuggling and the growing use of drones for hostile attacks.”
The company further pointed to “recent drone-related hostilities along the Cambodia-Thailand border” as underscoring the emerging threats in the region.
IWI unveiled ARBEL in April 2024, and called it the “world’s first-ever revolutionary computerized small arms system” that was “poised to re-defined combat effectiveness.”

Chevrolet Camaro ZL1 Races BMW M4 Coupe From 45 MPH, Someone Is Going to Be Pretty Happy About It
10 photos
Photo: Import 2 Race / YouTube
Over the past few weeks, we have been patiently waiting for what feels like a decidedly long time for the good folks over at the racing-focused ' Import 2 Race ' channel on YouTube to return to their traditional venue - Island Dragway in Great Meadows, New Jersey. Nope, not yet, not a chance.
Unfortunately, there’s still no sign of going back to their home racetrack where quarter-mile dragstrip action is always feisty. Instead, they remain passionate about roll races – initially, we have been treated to a bunch of 65-mph roll race battles, with all the high-speed ‘drama’ happening at the iconic Pocono Raceway , a 2.5-mile tri-oval track in Blakeslee, Pennsylvania.
However, just recently, the videographer made a change of scenery – though not of the race format. So, they’re still not back at Island Dragway, but at least they are much closer to home now. They have shot a few cool brawls taking place during the 2026 Sunday Funday Mod2Fame event, and the action took place at an airport in Sullivan County, New York.
The format there is the 45-mph roll race variety since the strip isn’t as long as the straight at Pocono to allow higher start speeds. They also lack the RaceMotive infrastructure, so there’s no electronic scoreboard, and there’s no way of knowing the actual roll speeds. Instead, we have to rely on good old direct observational skills.
At least the protagonists have been pretty straightforward about the races, avoiding the pesky photo finishes. And we also saw a nice lot: a crimson Ford Mustang Dark Horse of the S650 iteration, the C8 generation of the Chevrolet Corvette ZR1, and even an old Cadillac CTS-V that tried to keep up with a twin-turbo C8 Chevrolet Corvette Z06 without turning green with envy.
Recently, the skirmish video focused on a Blue Oval representative: a light blue Ford Mustang Shelby GT500 that raced both a Chevrolet Camaro and a Callaway C8 Chevrolet Corvette build and came out on top in both cases. Now it’s time to switch the perspective to a dark blue Chevrolet Camaro ZL1 powered by a 6.2-liter LT4 supercharged V8 producing 650 hp and 650 lb-ft (881 Nm) of torque without breaking a sweat.
Its opponent isn’t something to be trifled with, either, since it’s a black BMW M4 Coupe with amber LED daytime running lights and those humongous kidney grilles looking ready to swallow the big American muscle car whole if it catches it off-guard. Only that it didn’t, and while the GM representative clearly wasn’t as planted as the Bavarian coupe on the unprepped surface, it still managed to prevail – winning the race ever so slightly, probably by less than a car’s length. Cool, right?

Hyundai Australia has announced the special BLK Edition versions for the smaller Kona Hybrid and the larger Tucson Hybrid crossover SUVs for customers across the Land Down Under.
The South Korean automaker Hyundai has been pretty busy internationally this fall with the signing of a multi-year agreement as the Official Automotive Partner of the UEFA Champions League (September), the international launch of the global version of the bold new Tucson compact crossover SUV (October at the Paris Motor Show), or the rise of Hyundai Motor to the 29th place in Interbrand’s “Best Global Brands 2026” ranking.
However, they also had time for the local and regional affairs. In Australia, for example, the 2027 Hyundai Staria Load Electric commercial van debuted at Everything Electric Sydney in late September; the Ioniq 6 N was awarded Gold at the 2026 Australian Good Design Awards in the Automotive and Transport Product category in October; the Fremantle Dockers and Hyundai signed a three-year partnership for the AFL and AFLW teams that same month, and also launched the i30 Sedan N Monochrome limited edition.
Now it’s time for yet another special series in November – or even two. More precisely, both the Hyundai Kona subcompact and Tucson compact crossover SUVs gain BLK Editions that “bring exclusive dark treatments to Hyundai’s most popular models,” with deliveries kicking off before the end of the month starting from AU $42,600 for Kona BLK and AU $51k for the Tucson BLK, which is the equivalent of almost $30k and about $36k at the current exchange rate, respectively.
While the 2026 Hyundai Kona is still pretty new, as the second generation was launched in late 2022 for the 2023 model year, unfortunately the 2026 Tucson is at the end of its life for the NX4 fourth generation, which came to life in 2020. As such, the new BLK Edition serves as a sort of swan song for the NX4, and Hyundai says the special edition is limited to just 750 units for the Tucson CUV to enhance its exclusivity.
Both special editions are based on the respective Hyundai Kona and Tucson Elite trim models, but add bespoke “dark exterior styling elements combined with additional creature comforts to enhance appeal.” They are both offered solely with the 2WD hybrid powertrains and a “limited selection of exterior colors, designed to accentuate the black exterior accents.”
“We’re excited to introduce BLK Editions, which bring a more distinctive and contemporary dark edge to our most popular SUV models,” said Hyundai Motor Company Australia Chief Operating Officer, Gavin Donaldson. “With black-finished wheels and exterior trim, paired with cabin enhancements, BLK Editions give customers a bold new expression of style while delivering the comfort, technology and practicality that define the Hyundai SUV line-up.”
The Hyundai Kona BLK Edition adds, above the Elite, a 12.3-inch digital cluster, black exterior styling, Navigation, the Bose Premium Audio, as well as 18-inch black alloy wheels. The Tucson, meanwhile, receives 19-inch black alloy wheels and the Bose system, along with black exterior details.
The available premium colors are Ecotronic Grey, Abyss Black, Ultimate Red, and Denim Blue Mica, alongside the standard Atlas White for the Kona. The Tucson receives the standard Pearl White Mica, as well as the premium Olivine Grey Metallic, Space Black Metallic, Ruby Luxe Metallic, and Stormy Sea Metallic. Cool or not?

Talon’s Eagle nickel-copper mine in northern Michigan. Credit: Talon Metals.
By: Denise Heckbert November 4, 2026
Michigan is backing a new copper and nickel push near Lake Superior even as it continues cleaning up pollution left by the last mining boom.
Perseverance Metals (TSXV: PMI) announced a nickel-copper sulphide discovery in September, while Talon Metals (TSX: TLO; US-OTC: TLOFF) reported a mineralized magmatic conduit at its Roland target in October. Highland Copper (TSXV: HI; US-OTC: HDRSF) was awarded a $50-million (C$71-million) state grant in August for its Copperwood project.
“When you come in as a new operator, it’s like ‘trust us it’s going to be great, don’t worry about it,’” Talon CEO Darby Stacey told The Northern Miner . “But mining’s got enough of a reputation and a legacy where that’s not good enough.”
The region once supplied 96% of U.S. copper. At Torch Lake, copper still contaminates sediments about six decades after mining ceased. With exploration accelerating and proposed mines advancing near a lake that holds nearly 10% of the world’s surface fresh water, Michigan’s rules for modern mines could soon face a test across an entire district.
Environmental footprint
Indigenous peoples had mined and used copper on the Keweenaw Peninsula for more than 7,000 years, including float copper, loose pieces of native copper carried and deposited by glaciers.
The native copper industry declined as lower-cost western mines took market share, although the White Pine sulphide mine farther west continued until 1997. About 181 million tonnes of stamp sands and other tailings were deposited in Torch Lake, displacing about 20% of its original volume.
Copper concentrations in Torch Lake sediments were about 200% higher than in a nearby reference lake, with all measurements exceeding a threshold for predicted harmful effects by at least ninefold, researchers including scientists from the U.S. Geological Survey found in a 2025 study . Concentrations in larval insects were 160% higher, underscoring copper’s persistence in the food web.
Talon’s Eagle mine is the only operating primary nickel mine in the U.S. and the first operation permitted under Michigan’s Part 632 nonferrous metallic mining law. Commercial production began in 2014. Lundin Mining (TSX: LUN), which acquired Eagle in 2013, operated it until Talon bought the mine and Humboldt Mill in January. Talon plans to use the mill to process ore from its Tamarack project in Minnesota.
Getting Eagle into production was contentious. Researchers writing in Resources Policy in November 2025 documented legal challenges between 2006 and 2014 by environmental groups and the Keweenaw Bay Indian Community. Opponents set up a month-long protest camp in May 2010, and about 500 community members demonstrated at the state capital as they challenged the permitting process.
Cleanup and trust
The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency added Torch Lake to the Superfund National Priorities List in 1986. The cleanup has included covering more than 900 acres (364 hectares) with topsoil and vegetation to reduce exposure to mining waste and limit erosion into nearby rivers and lakes, Scott Dean, a spokesperson for the Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy, said by email.
“There are indications that the Torch Lake macroinvertebrate community is bouncing back,” Dean said. The department remains concerned about how long full restoration of the lake’s sediments could take, he added.
“How do you establish trust?” Stacey said. “We’re going to do all the sampling per the regulation but who’s to say, ‘we’re going to trust the company’s numbers, we are going to trust that those are all the right sampling spots,’ those types of things? Before you’ve been there, been a good operator, there’s just a lot of uncertainty.”
Eagle provides up to $300,000 a year for an independent Community Environmental Monitoring Program. The Superior Watershed Partnership and the Keweenaw Bay Indian Community carry out the monitoring, while the Community Foundation of Marquette County manages the funding at arm’s length.
The program says there have been no state permit violations at Eagle or Humboldt. The Resources Policy researchers found that local attitudes towards Eagle had shifted from early opposition towards conditional acceptance, tied in part to independent monitoring and the operation’s environmental record.
New concerns
The historical Keweenaw boom focused largely on native copper, metal occurring in nearly pure form. Eagle and the new generation of nickel-copper targets are magmatic sulphide systems. Their sulphur-bearing minerals can generate acidic drainage if exposed to air and water.
“You know there are multiple ways where you can store tailings, high sulphide tailings, and have those be environmentally safe,” Stacey said. “One of the great ways to do it is to use an old pit, so they aqueously store that taking oxygen out of the equation and stopping that reaction before it happens.”
Humboldt stores sulphide-bearing tailings underwater in a former open pit, limiting their exposure to oxygen. The Keweenaw Bay Indian Community said in a 2025 update that it supported Eagle’s proposal to use more tailings as underground backfill, which would reduce the amount stored at surface.
The community’s Natural Resources Department said in July it had begun a state-funded baseline metals study at 19 stream sites in three watersheds to establish natural ranges before more mining takes place. The work is expected to continue through September 2027.
District-wide test
An April technical report extended Eagle’s reserve-backed mine plan into the second half of 2030, largely through the Keel deposit. Talon reported a mineralized magmatic conduit at Roland in October and is drilling Boulderdash as part of a 1,600-sq.-km Upper Peninsula exploration package.
Copperwood is the only other Upper Peninsula project to have received a Part 632 mining permit, although the state lists it as issued and still awaiting effect. Highland received a non-binding $250-million letter of interest from the U.S. Export-Import Bank in September 2025 towards an estimated $400-million initial capital requirement. Protect the Porkies, a local opposition group named after the nearby Porcupine Mountains, is challenging the state grant in court.
Perseverance completed a C$11.8-million ($8.42-million) private placement on Oct. 2, less than a month after its Voyageur discovery. The financing gives the company at least 12 to 18 months to trace the mineralization towards a potential sulphide deposit, CEO Michael Tucker said in an interview.
“The good thing is with this style of deposit, if you can get to where you’ve demonstrated economic grade, you can get to actual deposit definition pretty quick,” Tucker said.
White Pine North
Kinterra Capital submitted a Part 632 mining permit application in September for White Pine North and released a prefeasibility study the same month. It outlined a 26-year mine plan, initial capital costs of $905.5 million and an after-tax net present value of $1.38 billion at an 8% discount rate.
Part 632 requires groundwater and surface water monitoring during operations and for 20 years after mining ends. The state can extend monitoring in 20-year increments if contamination risk remains. With Copperwood holding a permit, White Pine North under review and exploration accelerating, the rules that have governed a single operating nonferrous mine could soon apply across the district.
“I’d rather not see anybody come in there with fairly good financial backing and start making a mess of things,” Tucker said. “But, I don’t think it’s going to happen. I think the way the younger crowd is now, I suspect we’re all trying to do things the right way.”

Aerial view of the Fen project area. Credit: Rare Earths Norway.
Posted By: FREDERIC TOMESCO November 4, 2026
Privately held developer Rare Earths Norway approved construction of a €24-million (C$38 million) pilot plant to test processing of material from its Fen project, advancing efforts to turn Europe’s largest documented rare earths deposit into a source of permanent-magnet ingredients.
The facility in Ulefoss, about 160 km southwest of Oslo, is scheduled to start operating in the third quarter of 2027, the company said Tuesday . Funding includes €5.4 million from Innovation Norway and €1.9 million from the Telemark Development Fund. Other contributions weren’t specified.
“This investment is a concrete step towards bringing the Fen deposit into production,” Rare Earths Norway CEO Håvard Moe said in the statement. “The pilot will allow us to validate our processing route, generate essential operating data and supply rare earth products to European partners for test production of metal and magnets.”
News of the investment comes as European Union (EU) member countries step up efforts to cut their dependence on Chinese rare earths and magnets. Fen holds neodymium and praseodymium – two rare earth elements that are used in powerful magnets for electric vehicles, wind turbines and defence equipment, giving the project significance beyond Norway.
“Europe’s dependence on imported rare earths is a strategic vulnerability we can no longer afford to ignore,” Bernd Schäfer, CEO of the Berlin-based EIT RawMaterials consortium, said in the statement. EIT, an EU-backed raw materials innovation network, is providing funding for the Norwegian project.
Integrated route
Rare Earths Norway aims to begin extracting rare earths commercially in the early 2030s.
Until then, the pilot plant will test an integrated route from ore to rare earth oxides, generate operating data and supply products to European partners for trial production of metals and magnets. It will sit inside an existing industrial building.
A resource update for Fen released in March outlined 123 million indicated tonnes grading 1.35% total rare earth oxides, containing about 1.7 million tonnes of oxides. Inferred resources totalled 1.08 billion tonnes grading 1.31%, containing 14.2 million tonnes. The resource has an effective Dec. 31 date.
Combined contained oxides rose about 80% from the 8.8 million tonnes reported in 2024. The estimate also established Fen’s first indicated resource, a category carrying greater geological confidence than inferred material. Neodymium and praseodymium oxides account for about 19% of total rare earth oxides in the indicated category.
The expansion reflected additional drilling and changes to Rare Earths Norway’s proposed mining approach. The company had analysed about 30,000 metres of drill core, including 10,000 metres from last year’s exploration campaign. Its design increased the protective rock layer between underground openings and the surface to 100 metres from 25 metres.
National interest
Norway’s government took over the zoning process in April because the development involves matters of national interest.
In September, the government set an ambition to complete the plan by 2028, preferably by the end of next year. The process will determine locations and conditions for underground mining, processing facilities, tailings storage and infrastructure.
A pilot application published by Norway’s Environment Agency in March envisaged processing 6,000 tonnes of ore over three years to optimize concentrate production.

Ocean Network Express (ONE) has doubled its full-year profit forecasts to $2bn, after more than quadrupling its net profit for the three months to September, amid a surge in rates and volumes.
Over the second quarter, July-October for the Singapore-based carrier, net profit hit $1.3bn, compared with just $285m, a year earlier, with revenue climbing 41% year on year, to $6.3bn.
CEO Till Ole Barrelet said: “The second quarter delivered a strong financial performance, contributing to a solid first half of FY2026, reflecting our team’s success in growing volumes and achieving higher utilisation, despite a challenging environment.
“Reflecting this positive momentum, we are pleased to raise full-year outlook to $2bn. Looking ahead, we will adapt our network in response to evolving conditions, with safety remaining our top priority.”
Much of the success can be put down to a an almost 50% year-on-year uptick in rates, from $1,252 per teu over the same period in 2025 to $1,709 this year, as well as a small bounce in volumes, to 3.4m teu, compared with 3.26m last year.
The strong Q2 showing marks a sharp contrast to a weak first quarter, raising profits for the six months to October to $1.34bn, compared with $371m over the same period in 2025, on the back of revenues of $10.8bn.
Despite the strength on the transpacific lane – supported by US inventory and data centre demand – as well as Latin American and intra-Asia lanes, the carrier is expecting an easing of spots during the second half as seasonal demand weakens.
The expectation is in no small part due to the less-encouraging picture developing on Asia-Europe routes, with the gradual return of Suez sailings adding pressure on rates just as demand appears to be weakening.
Nonetheless, ONE still expects rates to remain above levels predicted in its earlier forecast, foreseeing a modest increase ahead of Chinese New Year, although its outlook appears dependent on conditions in the Strait of Hormuz remaining unchanged.
“We remain focused on advancing our ONE2030 strategy, building on our strong foundation to deliver long-term value to customers and stakeholders,” Mr Barrelet said
As one of its three contributing shareholders, success for ONE had an effect on K Line’s first-half performance, the Japanese operator recording a massive 81.4% year-on-year uptick in H1 net profits, to $786m.
The company recorded $443m in equity earnings from unconsolidated subsidiaries and affiliates, of which ONE contributed $415m, although K Line chose to leave its full-year earnings forecast unchanged, projecting net profit of $1.2bn.
Meanwhile, Cosco Shipping Ports also reported this week, recording an 8.4% upturn in its third-quarter container throughput, which hit 42.3m teu, with revenue climbing 13%, to $484m, and gross profit increasing 19.3%, to $128m, over the quarter.
Nine months into 2026, Cosco’s ports division reported throughput up 8.1% on the same period of 2025, hitting 122.4m teu, while revenue rose 12.6%, to $1.39bn, generating a 19.7% increase in profit, to $316.3m.

A new integrated offering combining battery storage, energy trading and financing solutions for industrial sites
A solution already deployed at Saft’s Bordeaux site, reducing annual electricity costs by approximately 15%
Paris, November 4, 2026 – Saft, a wholly owned subsidiary of TotalEnergies and a global leader in advanced battery technology, launches EnerShift, an integrated solution that enables energy-intensive industries to finance, deploy, and optimize battery energy storage systems while unlocking additional value through energy market participation.
The solution combines battery storage technology, energy management expertise, financing options, and energy market optimization into a single integrated offering. Depending on customer requirements, Saft can support projects from initial feasibility studies and business case assessment through financing solutions, system deployment, and long-term operational optimization.
A key differentiator of the service is its ability to unlock additional value from battery assets through participation in electricity markets. By intelligently charging and discharging batteries according to market conditions, industrial sites can optimize energy purchasing, capitalize on price fluctuations, and capture the value of energy flexibility without adding operational complexity for site teams.
“Many industrial companies understand the operational benefits of energy storage, but financing and profitability often remain barriers to investment. Our objective is to help customers not only deploy battery systems but also maximize their economic return throughout the asset’s lifetime,” said Vincent Le Quintrec, ESS Sales Director at Saft.
The EnerShift model is already being demonstrated through Saft’s own industrial-scale project at its Bordeaux production site. The installation combines a 9 MWh battery energy storage system with advanced energy management and energy trading capabilities. By optimizing energy consumption and battery operation according to market conditions, the Bordeaux site has achieved annual electricity cost savings of approximately 15%. Combined with additional value created through electricity market participation, the project is expected to pay for itself in around five years, while strengthening operational resilience and advancing Saft’s decarbonization ambitions.
For industrial operators, these additional value streams can significantly improve project economics and shorten payback periods. Beyond reducing electricity costs, EnerShift helps turn battery storage into a strategic asset that enhances resilience, supports decarbonization, and creates lasting competitive advantage.
About Saft Saft is a global leader in high-performance battery technology, designing and manufacturing energy solutions for critical industrial applications. For more than 100 years, Saft has delivered reliable and sustainable systems used for safety, backup power, and mobility, on land, at sea, in the air, and in space.
Saft is a wholly owned subsidiary of TotalEnergies, a multi-energy company that produces and markets energy in all its forms worldwide.

source_document.body:
PARIS — U.S.-based naval drone maker Saildrone has picked Norwegian naval builder Umoe Mandal to produce the Surveyor multipurpose surveillance craft locally, with an eye on new sales in Northern Europe, company executives said.
The Norwegian shipbuilder, headquartered on the country’s southern tip reaching into the North Sea, specializes in composite structures for the naval sector, including masts for British Type 26 frigates. CEO Tom Fidjeland told reporters at the Euronaval trade show here that taking on the work of churning out Surveyors was “technically not difficult,” with a first mold already being readied.
“Mandal’s role in producing the Surveyor will strengthen Europe’s maritime defense industrial base and support the delivery of sovereign maritime domain awareness capabilities to Northern European navies,” Saildrone said in a statement.
The U.S. company will provide its autonomy suite, navigation, electronics and surveillance technology to be mounted on the Norwegian-built Surveyor bodies, the plan goes.
The Surveyor drone is 20 meters long, powered by a diesel motor and wind — a sail-like structure 13 meters high that also houses the onboard electronics. Saildrone markets the vehicle, which can be left alone cruising the ocean for up to 100 days, as a data collector on adversaries and maritime conditions. Multiple drones can be networked to increase the coverage area, according to the manufacturer.
Saildrone’s lineup also includes the smaller Explorer and Voyager models, as well we the larger Spectre, a weapons-capable version still in development.
The partnership comes as the U.S. company has positioned itself to sell naval drones to European navies keen on policing their territorial waters, including in the Baltic and North seas as well as Arctic locales.
Saildrone’s managing director for Europe, Robert Kleist, cited an alliance of Northern European nations Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway and Sweden, NORDEFCO for short, as a potential business generator for naval drones. The pact entails an acquisition track that could spin out national task orders for unmanned platforms, for which Saildrone would then compete, Kleist said.
Umoe Mandall CEO Fidjeland said his company will build a new production site near its main plant devoted to cranking out Surveyors, with an initial production rate of at least two per month.
In October, Saildrone announced a yearlong maritime surveillance mission involving four Voyager drone for the Swedish Navy. Denmark, which straddles the North and Baltic seas, a key transit route for Russian warships heading to the open Atlantic, has been using the craft since 2025.
Saildrone announced a European headquarters in Copenhagen in August, noting plans for an expanded drone production footprint in Europe. Besides Norway, those entail making Spectre boats in the Netherlands at yacht maker Van Der Valk Shipyard, and Surveyor wings in Poland, Saildrone founder and CEO Richard Jenkins said then.

BMW Honors Alex Zanardi With One-Off M3 Sports Sedan
12 photos
Photo: BMW Italy
The current M3 may be on its deathbed, with BMW prepping its successor as we speak, but it remains in production, and was just used by the company’s Italian arm to create a very special one-of-a-kind example.
Developed in partnership with Barromeo DeSilva, which is the design studio that oversaw the stylistic concept of the car, it marks what would have been the 60th birthday (October 23) of the late Alessandro Zanardi, as well as the 40th of the M3. The “Tribute to Alex Zanardi” is a bespoke creation based on the current M3, which features a very special look on the outside.
The livery is a reinterpretation of the BMW M colors, and a distinctive element mentioned by the automaker is the pineapple, Zanardi’s historic lucky charm, which is said to have been “ reinterpreted for the occasion" via the “ design language, ” and “ integrated into the car as a recognizable symbol of his positive spirit and his ability to face challenges with optimism and determination. ”
BMW hasn’t drawn the line here, because there are a few special touches on the inside, too. Here, the pictured M3 benefits from Alcantara upholstery on the seats with an anthracite look. There are laser perforations, too, and you can see more of the BMW M colors here, which were again reinterpreted to feature a gradient pattern that morphs from blue to red. According to the automaker, the cockpit of the one-off G80 M3 pays tribute to the E30 M3 Sport Evolution.
Photo: BMW Italy “ Telling what Alex meant to BMW and all those who had the privilege of sharing a stretch of the road with him is much more complex. Because his memory continues to be extraordinarily alive, ” said President and CEO of BMW Italy, Sergio Solero. “ Alex taught us that we are not defined by what happens to us, but by what we choose to do with what we have, ” the exec added. “ This BMW M3 Tribute was born with precisely this spirit. ”
Alex Zanardi was born in Bologna, Italy, on October 23, 1966, and he had a career in the minor formulas and in Formula 1. He won the CART World Series in 1997 and 1998, and in 2001, on September 15, he was involved in a serious crash at the Lausitzring circuit, resulting in the amputation of both legs. This sparked the second phase of his racing career, during which he became a symbol of resilience and determination.
Zanardi returned to the world of motorsport in the 2003 European Touring Car Championship, driving for BMW Team Italy Spain, and he then became a BMW Motorsport driver in this FIA WTCC from 2005 to 2009, scoring four overall victories . He also drove a Z4 GT3 in the 24 Hours of Spa in 2015, won the Italian GT Championship with an M6 GT3 in 2016, made a guest appearance in DTM in 2018 with an M4 DTM, and drove in the 24 Hours of Daytona. He passed away on May 1, 2026.
Before wrapping it up, we will remind you that the G80 BMW M3 Sedan is now six years old, and was facelifted in 2022 for the 2023 model year, getting updates both inside and out, and under the hood. The four-door sedan is joined by a five-door station wagon, which adds the Touring suffix, and features the same goodies as its shorter-roof sibling.
Photo: BMW Italy The most basic version of the model has 473 horsepower from its twin-turbocharged 3.0-liter twin-turbocharged inline-six, taking 4.1 seconds to hit 60 mph (97 kph) from zero. The Competition model remains rear-wheel drive, and brings 503 horsepower to the output party, dropping the acceleration time to 3.8 seconds. As its name implies, the Competition xDrive is all-wheel drive. It has 523 hp on tap from an updated version of the same engine, and drops the sprint time to 3.4 seconds.
A brand new BMW M3 Sedan will set you back a minimum of $79,300 in the United States of America, excluding destination, options, and dealer fees. The mid-range Competition has an MSRP of $83,500 attached to it, and the M3 Competition xDrive starts at $88,600. The M3 Touring is not on sale in the States.
Reports indicate that the new-generation BMW M3 will launch in 2028, joining the mechanically-unrelated M3 Electric, which is apparently due a few months from now. The next M3 (ICE) is expected with a 3-liter twin-turbo inline-six, perhaps with mild-hybrid assistance, and details surrounding the output and thrust are unknown. Nevertheless, it should offer over 600 horsepower at a hard push of the right pedal in order get in line with its Audi RS 5 and Mercedes-AMG C 63 rivals.
The next-gen BMW M3 lineup will comprise the M3 Sedan and M3 Touring, and we do not expect to see the latter in dealers across the United States. Mind you, the larger M5 Touring is being sold over here, from $125,300 (MSRP), alongside the M5 Sedan, and the facelifted iteration, which will step into the Neue Klasse realm, will continue to be offered on our shores.

It’s a battle of the numbers, with both Novo and Eli Lilly claiming superiority in the early oral GLP-1 race. But who is right? Novo CEO Mike Maziar Doustdar insists his rival doesn’t have all the data.

Range Rover Abandoning Its Entry Models, Evoque and Velar To Be Discontinued in 2027
36 photos
Photo: Land Rover
Somewhat unsurprising, Range Rover has decided that cheaper SUVs are not worth its effort. Both the front-biased Evoque and the rear-biased Velar are supposed to leave the lineup by the end of 2027 with no direct successors in sight, ending a chapter in which the luxury-oriented marque attracted customers who could not justify spending Range Rover Sport or Range Rover money.
Instead of replacing those models, Jaguar Land Rover is moving Range Rover upmarket while letting the Defender and Discovery lines handle lesser customers. Martin Limpert, namely the managing director of Range Rover, told Autocar that giving Defender and Discovery clearer positions in the market pretty much sealed the fates of the Evoque and Velar.
This decision follows the group's House of Brands reorganization, whose main target is differentiation. Taking a step back, it's easy to understand the business calculation behind it. JLR wants Range Rover to continue printing money, concentrating on expensive vehicles with greater margins instead of stretching the badge to capture more customers.
The Defender and Discovery brands will take care of said customers. However, the Evoque is a pretty interesting casualty because this model alone took Range Rover to completely new heights. At its peak, the Evoque helped Land Rover move over 434,000 units globally, with the Evoque accounting for more than a third of global deliveries.
To understand how big the Evoque was a decade ago, the Halewood factory had to move to a 24-hour production schedule to keep up with demand. Its distinctive styling, compact footprint, and desirable badges made it a hit with people who always wanted to join the Range Rover club without the size and expense of larger models like the Sport.
Photo: Land Rover The Velar followed as a larger, more expensive alternative. Even more dynamic than the Evoque from the standpoint of styling, the rear-biased model never reached the commercial heights of the lesser sibling. Its annual sales peaked at roughly half those of its brother. Said models retail at 44,855 and 56,740 pounds sterling in the UK, and neither starting price fits the direction R R wants to take.
Scheduled to hit dealers in 2027, the all-new GT is a road-focused Range Rover that is expected to be priced in the ballpark of 90,000 pounds sterling. This fellow is the first JLR model to feature Electrified Modular Architecture underpinnings, and JLR will assemble it at the factory where the outgoing Evoque is made. Halewood is also responsible for the outgoing Land Rover Discovery Sport.
In any case, a pricing difference this large between the current entry-level models and the GT is definitely going to change things at Range Rover. Whether they'll change for the better or worse, it's hard to tell right now. Limpert, meanwhile, told Autocar that more than 80 percent of interest for the GT comes from customers who currently own vehicles from other brands.
Expressing interest in something one would like to purchase at some point in the future and a clear intent of putting money down right now on the GT are two very different things, though. And furthermore, there is no other number attached to that 80 percent mentioned by Limpert.

VIENNA — U.K-based Babcock International has launched Pelorus, a digital platform intended to connect warship construction, operations and maintenance data.
The British defense and engineering company announced the launch Nov. 3 at the Euronaval defense trade show in Paris, saying the platform already operates in selected Babcock-managed maritime construction and support environments. Babcock did not identify the deployments or customers involved, or provide figures showing how the platform has affected fleet availability or maintenance costs.
According to the company, Pelorus combines information from multiple systems to track shipbuilding progress, commissioning and trials, fleet availability, maintenance and logistics.
“The future of maritime capability depends on the ability to connect design, production, operational and support data into a single digital environment,” said Nick Hine, Babcock’s chief growth officer and marine chief executive, in the announcement.
The company positioned the platform as supporting both existing fleets and future combinations of crewed and autonomous vessels, linking it to its ARMOR Force concept − short for Autonomous and Remote, Maritime Operational Response Force. Babcock said Pelorus could also be adapted for other defense and critical infrastructure applications.
Babcock’s naval business spans shipbuilding and long-term fleet support. The company is building five Type 31 frigates for Britain’s Royal Navy at its Rosyth yard in Scotland. It also maintains and upgrades British nuclear-powered submarines at Devonport and Clyde, according to its website .

Image: AI-generated
By Alex Lennane
4 November 2026
There is no shortage of companies enjoying the AI boom – from airports to airlines and forwarders, the latest airfreight trend is filling both aircraft and coffers – but companies are now trying to find a way to prove their competitive edge in the market, whether by handling, network, or capacity.
Expeditors yesterday reported record third-quarter airfreight tonnage, up approximately 13% year on year, with hyperscaler demand a significant driver of the growth. Group revenue rose 42%, to $4.1bn, while net earnings climbed 55%, to $345m.
That demand also included shipments from Tier 1 and Tier 2 suppliers supporting AI infrastructure, the forwarder noted, extending the business beyond finished servers into the wider manufacturing supply chain.
“Air capacity remains constrained by limited fleet expansion and new aircraft delivery delays,” it said, adding that demand continued to outpace available capacity, keeping rates elevated.
However, today’s TAC Index update shows differing conditions across tradelanes.
Its global Baltic Air Freight Index slipped 1.1% in the week to 2 November, but remained 22.8% above a year earlier. China-US rates continued to rise strongly, while rates from Taiwan also increased and rates from Vietnam eased slightly.
The operational challenges behind this growth were evident in interviews at TIACA’s Air Cargo Forum in Miami last week, where Changi Airport highlighted the need to protect high-value equipment throughout its journey, including the short transfer between warehouse and aircraft.
Jaisey Yip, the airport group’s cargo business division VP, told The Loadstar that much of the airport’s cargo growth this year had come from semiconductors and AI-related infrastructure. Throughput reached approximately 1.66m tonnes in the first nine months, up 8.5% year on year.
But capturing that business required more than flight connection, she said.
“Not only are the shipments high-value, they are time-critical, and also shock- and vibration-sensitive,” she added, and p roduction equipment could also be outsized and require main-deck freighter capacity.
To address the handling risks, Changi’s partner, SATS, had recently trialled and introduced a suspension-enabled pallet dolly, designed to reduce shock, vibration, and tilt during airside transfers.
Ms Yip said Changi was positioning itself “ not only to facilitate our key exports, but also to facilitate hi-tech trades around the region to the rest of the world”.
Emirates SkyCargo is also targeting the sector, yesterday launching AI Tech, a dedicated product for server racks, semiconductors, GPUs, capital equipment, and other AI hardware.
The product combines priority loading, standardised handling procedures, and shipment monitoring through the carrier’s Dubai command centre. Expert project cargo support is available for oversized and heavy shipments, while highly specialised manufacturing equipment requires advance assessments of station capabilities.
“In July alone, we transported more than 700 tonnes of AI infrastructure across our global network, and demand has continued to grow,” said divisional SVP Badr Abbas.
Emirates said tall, dense server racks often weighed more than 3.5 tonnes, underlining the importance of main-deck capacity alongside the passenger belly network.
The demand is also generating multiple airfreight movements before equipment reaches its final installation.
Atlas Air’s Martin Drew described a two-stage supply chain, with components flown from Asian manufacturing centres to assembly locations, including Guadalajara in Mexico, before completed server racks were distributed worldwide.
“You’ve got semiconductors, chips, motherboards, and GPUs coming predominantly out of Asia into places such as Guadalajara in Mexico, where factories assemble these server racks. Then the server racks are sent all over the world,” he told The Loadstar .
The destination market extends beyond the US. Avianca Cargo CEO Diogo Elias said the airline was moving server racks from Miami into South American markets like Brazil, Uruguay, Paraguay, and Chile.
The height of the equipment – typically around 90 inches (228.6cm), he said, which made freighter main decks important for those shipments.
However, while the initial infrastructure build-out is creating substantial demand, airlines are also considering what the next phase will require.
Mr Drew said rapid technological development supported recurring replacement business.
“The technology is evolving so quickly. We hear anything from 18 months to three years, when that server rack becomes effectively obsolete and needs to be replaced.”
LATAM Cargo group CEO Andrés Bianchi, whose airline also carries AI-related cargo, raised a question about the physical form those replacement shipments would take. He wondered: “What happens when the data centre is built, and what you’re going to replace is not the rack itself, but the processor?
“Are you going to send racks again?”
For airlines planning capacity around today’s demand, continued spending on AI would not necessarily produce the same mix of bulky racks, components, and manufacturing equipment.
“This is a big opportunity today,” said Mr Bianchi. “But you’ve got to think about what is the opportunity for the future, and how that can translate into other areas of the business.”

Without a doubt, the French automaker Renault succeeded in its plan to make its Romanian subsidiary a viable entry-level alternative to the established carmakers roaming across the Old Continent.
They took over Automobile Dacia back in late 1999 and immediately started chasing Volkswagen’s Skoda brand, which initially had the same customer targets. But while Dacia remained a smart choice over the years, Skoda has often surpassed the namesake Volkswagen brand in both sales and prices.
Today, Dacia is an innovator in the smart automotive area above all – they have a female CEO, which is still rare even in today’s business climate, and have continuously created success stories with models like the Logan, Sandero, Duster and, most recently, the Bigster. They are on their way toward attacking the compact class with both the Bigster and the new Striker, their biggest models to date.
But, of course, the bread and butter across the Old Continent remains the Dacia Sandero and Sandero Stepway series – the European sales leader in both 2024 and 2025! Just recently, Dacia made strides to retain the crown in 2026 with the introduction of the late-2025 mid-cycle refresh, the second facelift operated across the board.
Also, they just announced that the Old Continent's leading models will become even more enticing as both the Dacia Sandero and its Stepway version go hybrid with 155 ps or 153 hp on tap. They remain highly accessible, with prices in the UK starting from £17,995 (OTR) and £19,295 (OTR), which is about $24k or $26k at the current exchange rate, respectively. And they’re also feisty, hitting 62 mph in 8.3 seconds.
Anyway, the future is coming, and the rumor mill plus the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI are already thinking about the fourth iteration of the Dacia Sandero twins.
More precisely, Andrei Avarvarii, the virtual artist behind Avarvarii Automotive Artworks (also known as ' avarvarii ' on social media), has taken a thorough, in-depth CGI look at Dacia's upcoming plans and came up with this unofficial, hypothetical design project for the next-generation Sandero Stepway as an illustration for Auto Express.

It’s pretty obvious the pixel master has infused the fake next-gen Sandero Stepway with “a sharper, more futuristic edge (…) taking direct inspiration from the Striker alongside the brand's latest Bigster and Duster models.”
It’s also slightly more rugged, as per the trends, and in their opinion, it will have a “multi-energy platform supporting both full-electric and hybrid-petrol powertrains (so) the design projects a planted, purposeful road presence for Dacia's next chapter.” What do you think – yay or nay? Volkswagen Puts a Price Tag on the 2027 California, Here’s How Much the Campervan Costs
7 photos
Photo: Volkswagen
Having been unveiled earlier this year, when summer just kicked off in the northern hemisphere, the 2027 Volkswagen California is now available to order in the United Kingdom.
The tiny home on wheels is a 2026 model in continental Europe, but it is marketed as a 2027 model in the UK because while the order books have officially opened, the deliveries will commence early next year.
Mind you, the visual updates are not that dramatic to make you mistake it for an all-new ride, but they will definitely make it more noticeable. The biggest novelties revolve around the model’s front fascia, where it features a revised lighting signature, different headlights, and a new bumper that looks a lot cleaner this time around. And the headlights also shine brighter, according to the German car manufacturer.
The changes continue on the inside, where the latest iteration of the Volkswagen California benefits from a new dashboard panel that comprises a bigger 12.9-inch infotainment system with a free-standing display and a tablet-like design. There is also an upgraded digital gauge cluster, and the improved materials and decorative stitching are also part of the refresh.
Photo: Volkswagen Volkswagen also mentions the power latching sliding doors and tailgate, as well as the new wheel designs, which range from 17 to 19 inches in diameter. A new electric stationary air conditioning system is also on deck, albeit on the eHybrid 4Motion model, which allows the campervan to be cooled, ventilated, and heated while it is charging for up to eight hours, and this makes it ideal for sleeping in comfort regardless of the outside weather.
The color palette has also been updated and now includes the Reed Green, Grey Brown, Grenadilla Black, and Sunset Red. All of these are metallic, and they are joined by the two-tone Grenadilla Black / Sunset Red, and Candy White / Grey Brown. The model can be specified in one of the 19 solid, two-tone, and metallic colors available, in addition to a black roof design, which is optional.
The latest generation of the Travel Assist system is on deck, and enables assisted lane changing on motorways on the 2027 Volkswagen California. Moreover, traffic light recognition is also on deck in a premiere. Integrated Emergency Assist is also included, guiding the vehicle to the hard shoulder or the outermost lane in case the driver suffers a medical emergency, and numerous other safety gizmos are also included.
But what about the pricing, you ask? Well, the most affordable version of the 2027 Volkswagen California in the United Kingdom is the Beach, equipped with a 2-liter TDI diesel engine. The mill is rated at 150 ps (148 hp/110 kW), and drives the front wheels through a seven-speed DSG automatic transmission. Pricing starts at 66,334 pounds (equal to $88,970), and it includes VAT and OTR costs.
Volkswagen’s 2027 California Beach is also available with the 1.5 eHybrid powertrain, which offers 245 ps (242 hp/180 kW), utilizes a six-speed DSG automatic transmission, and features 4Motion all-wheel drive. In this case, customers must fork out a minimum of 74,637 pounds ($100,110).
The Coast is next in line, and just like the lesser Beach variant, it utilizes the same powertrains . Pricing for the diesel-powered variant starts at 71,464 pounds ($95,855), and the electrified model is available from 79,672 pounds ($106,862).
Photo: Volkswagen Last but not least, the Ocean is the top trim level of the 2027 Volkswagen California in the UK. The diesel variant kicks off at 79,762 pounds ($106,980), and the hybridized one can be yours from a minimum of 87,970 pounds ($117,990).
Volkswagen’s 2027 California Ocean 150 PS 2.0 TDI 7-speed DSG is available on a 48-month contract with 10,000 miles (~16,000 km) per year with a deposit contribution of 5,000 pounds ($6,705), a customer deposit of 16,511.82 pounds ($22,147), and 47 monthly payments of 549 pounds ($736). The optional final payment is 44,253 pounds ($59,355).
The latest iteration of the camper van benefits from the company’s enhanced warranty and service plan, the 5+ Promise at no extra cost, which includes five services, three for electric models, three MOTs, and a five-year warranty and five years of roadside assistance.
In Germany, the VW California campervan in the Beach configuration has a starting price of 66,087 euros, which equals $73,945 at today’s exchange rate.
As for the larger and better-equipped Volkswagen Grand California , customers must choose between the 600, 680, Dune 600, and Dune 680 models. Pricing for the Grand California starts at 84,208 pounds ($112,945) OTR, including VAT for the most affordable version. The 680 model kicks off at 86,986 pounds ($116,670), the Dune 600 at 85,408 pounds ($114,555), and the Dune 680 at 88,186 pounds ($118,280), the brochure, which is available on the company’s official website (Vans) reveals.
So, is the 2027 Volkswagen California campervan your next home away from home? Or does the pricier and bigger Grand California sound better?

Dacia Sandero & Sandero Stepway, Europe's Best-Selling Model Series, Goes Hybrid With 153 HP on Tap
10 photos
Photo: Dacia
The Romanian automaker , a subsidiary of the French Renault Group, makes the Old Continent's leading models, the Dacia Sandero and Sandero Stepway, even more enticing from now on by adding the ‘hybrid 155’ version with a combined output of 155 ps or 153 hp.
It’s early November, and the automotive world is pretty busy with cool events: in Las Vegas, Nevada, the annual SEMA Show is gathering all the most exotic builds from both automakers and the aftermarket realm, and in Italy, EICMA, or the International Exhibition of Cycles, Motorcycles, and Accessories in Milan, gathers everything new on just two wheels.
However, quite obviously, the automotive wheel is also turning around them, and in places like Australia we have recently seen BMW announce the Nürburgring special edition is coming to the Land Down Under or Hyundai revealing the Kona and Tucson BLK limited series. Now it’s time to switch to the Old Continent, or the United Kingdom to be more precise, and see what’s new from Dacia.
The Romanian brand owned by Renault counts on the Dacia Sandero and Sandero Stepway series as Europe’s best-sellers, and both models now gain full hybrid power for the first time, “ringing greater efficiency, electric driving and automatic ease to two of the brand’s most accessible models.” In fact, with a combined output of 153 hp or 155 ps, they are bringing them into affordable ‘hot hatch’ territory for the first time, too.
The series is Europe’s best-selling passenger car in both 2024 and 2025, and most likely in 2026 too, and the Sandero and Sandero Stepway are now getting the Hybrid 155 powertrain from the larger models like Jogger, Duster, and Bigster that “can spend up to 80% of urban driving time in electric mode, with no need to plug in.”
They also say that “lively performance meets everyday efficiency,” sprinting to 62 mph or 100 kph in 8.3 seconds while potentially increasing the fuel efficiency by up to 40% compared to an equivalent petrol engine. The Sandero hybrid 155 will be priced from £17,995 on-the-road, and the Sandero Stepway hybrid 155 is available from £19,295 on-the-road, with both models ready for ordering starting in early November 2026.
That’s about $24k or $26k at the current exchange rate, which is great pricing, even for the UK, which is notoriously expensive when it comes to automobiles as of late. Already proven on the rest of the Dacia range, the hybrid 155 powertrain mixes a 1.8-liter four-cylinder petrol engine with two electric motors – a traction motor and high-voltage starter/generator – plus a 1.4kWh battery and an electrified automatic gearbox.
The system operates a clutchless transmission with four gears for the gasoline engine and two for electric operation, and there’s also regenerative braking. The Sandero hybrid 155 will be available in Expression and Journey trim levels, priced from £17,995 and £19,295 OTR, with the second one adding a seven-inch digital driver display, Media Nav Live with connected navigation and real-time traffic information, an Arkamys six-speaker 3D audio system, automatic AC, keyless entry, and a Multiview camera, and more above Expression.
The Dacia Sandero Stepway hybrid 155 is more rugged and gets the same Expression or a dedicated Extreme trim from £20,595 OTR, packing Extended Grip, a Multiview camera, Blind Spot Warning and Copper Brown exterior touches, among other things. The cars also have a maximum braked towing capacity of 1,100kg across both models, and Sandero Stepway packs a 200mm ground clearance.
“Sandero has always been about giving customers more of what they actually use, without making them pay for things they don’t. Hybrid 155 fits that thinking perfectly. It brings automatic driving, electric power around town, and lower fuel consumption, but there’s nothing extra to plug in or worry about. Whether you prefer the straightforward simplicity of Sandero or the more rugged character of Sandero Stepway, you now get those same useful hybrid benefits while keeping everything that makes each model such a strong Dacia,” says Lina Ribeiro, Dacia Brand Director for the UK .

Pfizer’s Valneva-partnered Lyme disease vaccine is nearing a regulatory submission, with interest in preventative options against the tick-borne disease rising around the world.
